### Intercom
**URL:** https://intercom.help/bsport-helpcenter/en/articles/9721753-reports-2-0

<div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>A new version of the reports has been released! The objective of this new version is to make readability and navigation easier for you on the reports so that you can easily find the exact piece of information you are looking for.</p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-callout" style="background-color:#e8e8e880;border-color:#73737633"><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>Until the 1st of October, you can switch back and forth between the old and new versions by clicking on the &quot;Back to old version&quot; button. However, changes made on one version <b>will not</b> appear on the other. </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>After this date, the old version will be permanently out of access. </p></div></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>Check below what is new with version 2.0</p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-heading intercom-interblocks-align-left"><h1 id="h_30d0ef97b6">All reports page</h1></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>On the first page, you will now see a better distribution of the reports&#x27; types, still sorted by their categories. </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-image intercom-interblocks-align-left"><a href="https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/1140175237/6519e24b15083d096d70049c/image.png?expires=1778852700&amp;signature=6569f674294bb10859ccd3d40567dfea066d69769df23df5b2fb0844efdc3e6e&amp;req=dSEjFsh5mINcXvMW1HO4zUEfYSlBUlTGUz08JYqylfCRwVbhvVcx6TmPcUfc%0AmFhIso1AGLtCZYSBpYk%3D%0A" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer nofollow noopener"><img src="https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/1140175237/6519e24b15083d096d70049c/image.png?expires=1778852700&amp;signature=6569f674294bb10859ccd3d40567dfea066d69769df23df5b2fb0844efdc3e6e&amp;req=dSEjFsh5mINcXvMW1HO4zUEfYSlBUlTGUz08JYqylfCRwVbhvVcx6TmPcUfc%0AmFhIso1AGLtCZYSBpYk%3D%0A" alt="" width="2836" height="1344"/></a></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>As before, you can search a report type by its name in the search bar to find it more easily </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-heading intercom-interblocks-align-left"><h1 id="h_37b9887e58">Report detail page</h1></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>Once you open a report type, you can navigate between different views. The views are made of : </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-unordered-nested-list"><ul><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>One default view</b>, that is always accessible and cannot be deleted. You can however edit the data displayed via the edit view form </p></div></li><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>All your migrated views</b> form the 1.0 version of the reports if you had created any for that report&#x27;s type. These views were renamed &quot;[Migrated] name&quot; for you to identify them. </p></div></li><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>All future views</b>, that you will create from the 2.0 version of the reports</p></div></li></ul></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-callout" style="background-color:#e8e8e880;border-color:#73737633"><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>Note that if you had created several versions of a report in the 1.0 version (e.g. several &quot;Basket&quot; reports), they are now all migrated as views in the report type &quot;Basket&quot;.<br/>Quickfilters, advanced filters, and date filters were all saved as well for every view</p></div></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>If you wish to create a new view of this report, for example to apply specific filters, click on the &quot;Add view&quot; button </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-image intercom-interblocks-align-left"><a href="https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/1142574818/d17c49ae64b95044265d020f/image.png?expires=1778852700&amp;signature=c7e619f746303f71930f9d950b3c1e1a46058d6a17ee87999a5504b25dbf6f4b&amp;req=dSEjFMx5mYleUfMW1HO4zTr%2FrmyGfNBL2v2Uo%2FI6KEqPx1WuQpfRpPBgkjaU%0ADp1jiUe7V%2FeLzNiBWc8%3D%0A" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer nofollow noopener"><img src="https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/1142574818/d17c49ae64b95044265d020f/image.png?expires=1778852700&amp;signature=c7e619f746303f71930f9d950b3c1e1a46058d6a17ee87999a5504b25dbf6f4b&amp;req=dSEjFMx5mYleUfMW1HO4zTr%2FrmyGfNBL2v2Uo%2FI6KEqPx1WuQpfRpPBgkjaU%0ADp1jiUe7V%2FeLzNiBWc8%3D%0A" alt="" width="2088" height="86"/></a></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><br/>Then name the view and click on confirm. The default view and all new views created display all available columns and data and have no quick or advanced filters. </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-subheading intercom-interblocks-align-left"><h2 id="h_f8aa8a7937">Advanced filters and general display</h2></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>If you wish to build a view that always displays only the data that you need, click on the &quot;Edit&quot; icon</p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-image intercom-interblocks-align-left"><a href="https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/1142586220/47d418e71c6cb892d04bdf18/image.png?expires=1778852700&amp;signature=5ca3e375185d9c0aca03c93650d353048fa8c92aab72224257ae180af316d72e&amp;req=dSEjFMx2m4NdWfMW1HO4zcHDc2ajCdSWOb%2Baj1XM5rkag1NaYwYP%2BN7GMiNc%0AsD7NDSG2EOS%2B3mT1v5g%3D%0A" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer nofollow noopener"><img src="https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/1142586220/47d418e71c6cb892d04bdf18/image.png?expires=1778852700&amp;signature=5ca3e375185d9c0aca03c93650d353048fa8c92aab72224257ae180af316d72e&amp;req=dSEjFMx2m4NdWfMW1HO4zcHDc2ajCdSWOb%2Baj1XM5rkag1NaYwYP%2BN7GMiNc%0AsD7NDSG2EOS%2B3mT1v5g%3D%0A" alt="" width="2082" height="146"/></a></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>From here you can decide to rename the view, apply Advanced filters, or select/unselect the columns you want to appear in the view. Then click on &quot;Save and Generate&quot;</p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-image intercom-interblocks-align-left"><a href="https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/1142588176/e9357952e9f2cf3b44386d04/image.png?expires=1778852700&amp;signature=48ad542016cd64885f401533a082eea18d1a98d1cff1221a4412fccc9b942ef2&amp;req=dSEjFMx2lYBYX%2FMW1HO4zTV0MjYtX8WsuadYac%2FG3gEEUt9Z878Mklqkch7M%0A5UvOUxzKg1oUDUjckTY%3D%0A" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer nofollow noopener"><img src="https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/1142588176/e9357952e9f2cf3b44386d04/image.png?expires=1778852700&amp;signature=48ad542016cd64885f401533a082eea18d1a98d1cff1221a4412fccc9b942ef2&amp;req=dSEjFMx2lYBYX%2FMW1HO4zTV0MjYtX8WsuadYac%2FG3gEEUt9Z878Mklqkch7M%0A5UvOUxzKg1oUDUjckTY%3D%0A" alt="" width="1564" height="1330"/></a></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-callout" style="background-color:#e8e8e880;border-color:#73737633"><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>Tip</b> : </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-unordered-nested-list"><ul><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>Advanced filters</b> are made to be permanently applied to your view and to be really specific thanks to and/or rules management. <div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>Once your Facebook Pixels account and Google Tag Manager are linked, you will now be able to create GTM tags, linking them to a Pixel to track activity on Facebook Pixels. To learn how to link both accounts, <a href="https://intercom.help/bsport-helpcenter/en/articles/7860900-linking-pixels-and-google-tag-manager-gtm">check this article</a>.</p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b><i>First things first:</i></b></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>To allow Pixels to track events that happen on the bsport platform, you need to go through Google Tag Manager. That&#x27;s why you connected Google Tag Manager and Pixels in the previous step.</p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>You also need to make Google Tag Manager understand the events that happen on the bsport platform so that it can send them to Pixels.</p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>It is necessary <a href="https://intercom.help/bsport-helpcenter/en/articles/7854066-how-to-configure-a-google-analytics-variable-gtm">to create a variable on Google Tag Manager</a> which corresponds to the bsport event.</p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>Find all the bsport events here: <a href="https://pastebin.pl/view/23083ef7" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">https://pastebin.pl/view/23083ef7</a></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>We are now going to create the variable for a bsport event to be sent to Pixels.</p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>For this example we will choose the click on add to cart event.</p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>Let&#x27;s create the variable. In Google Tag Manager, go to Variables &gt; New.</p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-image intercom-interblocks-align-left"><a href="https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/533399550/09f9eec26e211a9edd597dd7/image.png?expires=1778852700&amp;signature=8de4dba34b85d6ac69c7b98c2df461b05fda1c8230f2371ce2a7458b27ac1214&amp;req=cSMkFcB3mIRfFb4f3HP0gF30MLnxxKhkX3M40hqZmbS9t3zYl5wlJlB2%2BRtU%0A3WWzHqN2c%2FGNA%2FIZKQ%3D%3D%0A" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer nofollow noopener"><img src="https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/533399550/09f9eec26e211a9edd597dd7/image.png?expires=1778852700&amp;signature=8de4dba34b85d6ac69c7b98c2df461b05fda1c8230f2371ce2a7458b27ac1214&amp;req=cSMkFcB3mIRfFb4f3HP0gF30MLnxxKhkX3M40hqZmbS9t3zYl5wlJlB2%2BRtU%0A3WWzHqN2c%2FGNA%2FIZKQ%3D%3D%0A" alt=""/></a></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>Then create a new variable &gt; Data Layer Variable.</p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>Put &quot;data&quot; in the name of the data layer variable. Name the variable, for us it will be &quot;dlv - data&quot;.</p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div <div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>N.B.: the screenshots in this sheet are from October 2020, the interface and the Facebook Pixels platform change regularly so the appearance may not be the same. Nevertheless, the process should remain the same.</b></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>First of all, what is Google Tag Manager?</b></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><i>Google Tag Manager (GTM) is a tag management system that allows you to track more advanced data. GTM quickly updates and facilitates the tracking of data on applications or websites. It is an interface that allows you to create and view the tags you create. GTM is a Tag Management System, and works like a CMS (Content Management System) except that it is not for site content but for special tags.</i></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>You can track your data by linking your Google Tag Manager account to Google Analytics for example.</p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>Why do we need Google Tag Manager?</b></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>The advantages of Google Tag Manager:</p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-unordered-nested-list"><ul><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>Saves time for developers. They don&#x27;t need to develop it in-house, understandable interface so anyone can implement it.</p></div></li><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>More accurate data. Allows for custom tracking, allows for analysis of specific data/needs.</p></div></li><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>Increases site speed (response time, workflow, page load time)</p></div></li></ul></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>Why set it up for your bsport account?</b></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><i>To be able to analyse the behaviour of students and potential students when they are on the bsport platform linked to your account. You can analyse the different steps, clicks, sessions and others.</i></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>What are Facebook Pixels?</b></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><i>The Facebook Pixel is a piece of code that allows you to retrieve data from users who have visited your website in order to build an audience.</i></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>Why do we need Facebook Pixels?</b></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><i>The Facebook Pixel is used to optimise advertising campaigns on Instagram and Facebook, to analyse traffic to your site via Facebook, and to track purchase path and other data related to advertising.</i></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>Why to set it up for its bsport account?</b></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><i>To be able to analyse the behaviour of users after clicking on a Facebook or Instagram ad. To have the right data to optimize your marketing campaigns.</i></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>You cannot apply tags from the Master Account, but the tags created from the Master Account are available to be used by any franchisee.</p></div><div system will start with <b>the first franchisee in alphabetical order</b>.</p></div></li><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>It will send the communication to all the members of this franchisee.</p></div></li><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>Then, the system will proceed to the take a look at the checklist below, as well as Apple and Google documentation:</p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>IMPORTANT TO CHECK :</b></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>👉🏽 <b>no special characters, weird lettering in the name and the description</b> 👉🏽 <b>no configured</p></div></li><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>[ ] Activities (or appointments) with both <b>pictures</b> and <b>description</b> your app name, subtitle, icon, description, screenshots, and more. Some of the key points are:</p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-unordered-nested-list"><ul><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>An app name can be up to 30 characters long and should be distinctive and avoid generic terms or names that are too similar to existing apps.</p></div></li><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>A subtitle can be up to 30 characters long and should summarize your app’s functionality in a concise phrase.</p></div></li><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>A full description can be up to 4000 characters long and should accurately describe your app’s functionality and content, highlight its benefits and features, and avoid misleading or irrelevant references, testimonials, or profanity.</p></div></li><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>An app icon should be simple, recognizable, and avoid graphic elements that may mislead users.</p></div></li></ul></div></li><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>For the <b>Google Playstore</b>, you can check out <a href="https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9859152?hl=en" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Create and set up your app</a>, which explains how to create your app and set it up using Play Console. You can also check out <a href="https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/13393723?hl=en" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Best practice for your store listing</a>, which provides tips and examples for creating your app title, description, icon, screenshots, and more. Some of the key points are:</p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-unordered-nested-list"><ul><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>An app title must be 30 characters or less and should be unique, accessible, and avoid common terms or profanity.</p></div></li><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>A short description should convey your app’s message in 80 characters or less and give users a summary of your app’s biggest benefits.</p></div></li><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>A full description should be 4000 characters or less and should describe your app’s functionality and content, highlight its features and value proposition, and avoid misleading or irrelevant references, testimonials, or profanity.</p></div></li><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin This ensures that developers have the necessary tools to test their apps and to maintain app quality and security standards.<b> Only the account owner </b>of the Google Developer Account (GDA) can complete this verification.</p></div></li></ul></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-subheading intercom-interblocks-align-left"><h2 id="h_81c0d02feb"><b>Step-by-Step Guide for Verification:</b></h2></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>1. Download the Google Play Console App on an Android Device:</b></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-unordered-nested-list"><ul><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>If the company owner (the owner of the GDA) doesn&#x27;t already have the Google Play Console app installed on their Android device, they will need to:</p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-unordered-nested-list"><ul><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>Scan the QR code shown in the image provided, or</p></div></li><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>Search for the Google Play Console app on the Google Play Store and download it manually.</p></div></li></ul></div></li></ul></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>2. Sign in to the Google Play Console App:</b></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-unordered-nested-list"><ul><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>Once the app is installed, they must sign in using the same Google account they are using for the Google Developer Account (the same email as shown in the instructions, e.g., <a href="mailto:google-developer-android-1@bsport.io" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">google-developer-android-1@bsport.io</a>).</b></p></div></li></ul></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>3. Verify Access to the Developer Account:</b></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-unordered-nested-list"><ul><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>After signing in, select the appropriate Developer Account (in this case, it should be the company account).</b></p></div></li><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>Follow the instructions that appear in the app to complete the verification process on the Android device.</p></div></li></ul></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-horizontal-rule"><hr/></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-subheading intercom-interblocks-align-left"><h2 id="h_9e416e209e"><b>What to Do if the Client Does Not Have an Android Device:</b></h2></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>If the client (the company owner) does not have access to an Android device, there are a few options:</p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>1. Use an Android Device Temporarily:</b></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-unordered-nested-list"><ul><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>The owner can borrow an Android device temporarily to complete the verification.</p></div></li><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>They would need to install the Google Play Console app, sign in with their account, and follow the same steps outlined above.</p></div></li></ul></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>2. Allow the Account Manager to Verify on Your Behalf:</b></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-unordered-nested-list"><ul><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>The owner can provide their Google Developer Account credentials to their bsport account manager, who can complete the verification on their behalf using an Android device.</p></div></li></ul></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>3. Purchase an Android Device:</b></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-unordered-nested-list"><ul><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>If the owner frequently needs to manage Android apps, it might be worth investing in a basic Android device to handle verifications, testing, and development.</p></div></li></ul></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>4. Contact Google Support:</b></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-unordered-nested-list"><ul><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>If none of the above options are feasible, the client can contact Google Support and explain that they do not have access to an Android device. Google may provide an alternative verification method or offer further guidance.</p></div></li></ul></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>5. Emulate Android:</b></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-unordered-nested-list"><ul><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>Another option is to use an Android emulator on a computer. Tools like Android Studio provide virtual devices that could potentially be used to run the Play Console app. However, this approach is less reliable and may not be officially supported by Google for ### Intercom
**URL:** https://intercom.help/bsport-helpcenter/en/articles/9888202-google-play-console-how-to-verify-android-device

<div class="intercom-interblocks-subheading intercom-interblocks-align-left"><h2 id="h_b8c4603e18"><b>Why is Google requesting Android mobile device verification?</b> </h2></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-unordered-nested-list"><ul><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>Google requires developers to verify that they have access to an Android mobile device in order to publish apps on Google Play. This ensures that developers have the necessary tools to test their apps and to maintain app quality and security standards.<b> Only the account owner </b>of the Google Developer Account (GDA) can complete this verification.</p></div></li></ul></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-subheading intercom-interblocks-align-left"><h2 id="h_c7452bfacb"><b>Step-by-Step Guide for Verification:</b></h2></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>1. Download the Google Play Console App on an Android Device:</b></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-unordered-nested-list"><ul><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>If the company owner (the owner of the GDA) doesn&#x27;t already have the Google Play Console app installed on their Android device, they will need to:</p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-unordered-nested-list"><ul><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>Scan the QR code shown in the image provided, or</p></div></li><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>Search for the Google Play Console app on the Google Play Store and download it manually.</p></div></li></ul></div></li></ul></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>2. Sign in to the Google Play Console App:</b></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-unordered-nested-list"><ul><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>Once the app is installed, they must sign in using the same Google account they are using for the Google Developer Account (the same email as shown in the instructions, e.g., <a href="mailto:google-developer-android-1@bsport.io" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">google-developer-android-1@bsport.io</a>).</b></p></div></li></ul></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>3. Verify Access to the Developer Account:</b></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-unordered-nested-list"><ul><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>After signing in, select the appropriate Developer Account (in this case, it should be the company account).</b></p></div></li><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>Follow the instructions that appear in the app to complete the verification process on the Android device.</p></div></li></ul></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-horizontal-rule"><hr/></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p> </p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-subheading intercom-interblocks-align-left"><h2 id="h_033a4204b2"><b>What to Do if the Client Does Not Have an Android Device:</b></h2></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>If the client (the company owner) does not have access to an Android device, there are a few options:</p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>1. Use an Android Device Temporarily:</b></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-unordered-nested-list"><ul><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>The owner can borrow an Android device temporarily to complete the verification.</p></div></li><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>They would need to install the Google Play Console app, sign in with their account, and follow the same steps outlined above.</p></div></li></ul></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>2. Allow the Account Manager to Verify on Your Behalf:</b></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-unordered-nested-list"><ul><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>The owner can provide their Google Developer Account credentials to their bsport account manager, who can complete the verification on their behalf using an Android device.</p></div></li></ul></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>3. Purchase an Android Device:</b></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-unordered-nested-list"><ul><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>If the owner frequently needs to manage Android apps, it might be worth investing in a basic Android device to handle verifications, testing, and development.</p></div></li></ul></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>4. Contact Google Support:</b></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-unordered-nested-list"><ul><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>If none of the above options are feasible, the client can contact Google Support and explain that they do not have access to an Android device. Google may provide an alternative verification method or offer further guidance.</p></div></li></ul></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p><b>5. Emulate Android:</b></p></div><div class="intercom-interblocks-unordered-nested-list"><ul><li><div class="intercom-interblocks-paragraph no-margin intercom-interblocks-align-left"><p>Another option is to use an Android emulator on a computer. Tools like Android Studio provide virtual devices that could potentially be used to run the Play Console app. However, this approach is less reliable and may not be officially supported by Google for verification purposes.</p></div></li></ul></div><section class="jsx-62724fba150252e0 related_articles my-6"><hr class="jsx-62724fba150252e0 my-6 sm:my-8"/><div class="jsx-62724fba150252e0 mb-3 text-xl
